article_title: Nurses' Experiences and Perceptions of Evidence-Based Healthcare Competence: A Qualitative Systematic Review.
citation: Hietaniemi, A.‐M., Ylimäki, S., Härkönen, H., Hannila, H.‐M., Tuomikoski, A.‐M., Oikarinen, A., Jansson, M., Pölkki, T., Kanste, O. & Kääriäinen, M. (2026). Nurses' Experiences and Perceptions of Evidence‐Based Healthcare Competence: A Qualitative Systematic Review. Journal of Advanced Nursing. https://doi.org/10.1111/jan.70399
title: JBI EBHC model: five sub‐dimensions of evidence‐based healthcare competence
description: The review organises nurses' EBHC competence using the JBI EBHC model framework (Jordan et al. 2019), which holds that evidence‐based practice "requires the integration of sub‐dimensions of EBHC (global health, evidence generation, evidence synthesis, evidence transfer and evidence implementation) into the healthcare system". The model defines EBHC competence for nurses as including knowledge, skills, values, attitudes, beliefs and experience. The review used the model's sub‐dimensions as the categorisation scheme for its meta‐aggregation of qualitative findings.
requirements: Nurses require competencies across all EBHC sub‐dimensions for the model to be realised in practice
constraints: In this review, no extracted findings were associated with the evidence synthesis sub‐dimension, so only four sub‐dimensions received synthesised findings
target_learning_goals: evidence‐based healthcare competence across global health, evidence generation, evidence synthesis, evidence transfer and evidence implementation
examples: The review categorised 89 extracted findings into 15 categories and four synthesised findings mapped onto the model's sub‐dimensions
key_sources: Hietaniemi, A.‐M., Ylimäki, S., Härkönen, H., Hannila, H.‐M., Tuomikoski, A.‐M., Oikarinen, A., Jansson, M., Pölkki, T., Kanste, O. & Kääriäinen, M. (2026). Nurses' Experiences and Perceptions of Evidence‐Based Healthcare Competence: A Qualitative Systematic Review. Journal of Advanced Nursing. https://doi.org/10.1111/jan.70399

article_title: Game-thinking; utilizing serious games and gamification in nursing education - a systematic review and meta-analysis.
citation: Nylén-Eriksen Mats, Stojiljkovic Marko, Lillekroken Daniela, Lindeflaten Katrin, Hessevaagbakke Elisabeth, Flølo Tone Nygaard, Hovland Olav Johannes, Solberg Ada Marie Svarstad Hansen Sylvia, Bjørnnes Ann Kristin, Tørris Christine. (2025). Game-thinking; utilizing serious games and gamification in nursing education – a systematic review and meta-analysis. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-024-06531-7
title: JBI critical appraisal checklists for RCT and quasi-experimental quality assessment
description: The Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) checklists were used to assess risk of bias and certainty of evidence. The article states that "The well-established JBI appraisal checklist for RCT´ (13 items), and the quasi-experimental checklist (9 items) assess internal validity". Studies were categorized as low quality when scoring < 50%, moderate quality with scores ≥ 50–70% and high when scoring > 70%.
requirements: Independent double-quality assessment by reviewers using the appropriate JBI checklist per study design
constraints: Quality categories are based on total scores: low < 50%, moderate 50–70%, high > 70%
key_sources: Nylén-Eriksen Mats, Stojiljkovic Marko, Lillekroken Daniela, Lindeflaten Katrin, Hessevaagbakke Elisabeth, Flølo Tone Nygaard, Hovland Olav Johannes, Solberg Ada Marie Svarstad Hansen Sylvia, Bjørnnes Ann Kristin, Tørris Christine. (2025). Game-thinking; utilizing serious games and gamification in nursing education – a systematic review and meta-analysis. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-024-06531-7

article_title: Screening, prevention, and management of patients with poststroke depression in a tertiary hospital in China: a best practice implementation project.
citation: Tan Jing, Brancatisano Olivia, Cadilhac Dominique A., Deng Bo, Wu Yanni, Li Yan, Liu Ning. (2023). Screening, prevention, and management of patients with poststroke depression in a tertiary hospital in China: a best practice implementation project. JBI Evidence Implementation. https://doi.org/10.1097/XEB.0000000000000377
title: JBI Evidence Implementation Framework: seven-stage audit-and-feedback approach with GRiP barrier analysis
description: The project was based on the JBI Evidence Implementation Framework, "which consists of seven stages, including first, identification of practice area for change; second, engaging change agents; third, assessment of context and readiness to change; fourth, review of practice against evidence-based audit criteria (baseline audit); fifth, implementation of changes to practice; sixth, reassessment of practice (follow-up audit); and seventh, consideration of the sustainability of practice changes." The GRiP matrix was used to identify barriers and match strategies, resources, and outcomes. The framework structured the three-phase project from January to June 2021.
requirements: A project team with defined roles and responsibilities, including organizational support from nursing leadership
Audit criteria derived from evidence summaries and guidelines, measured via documentation review, interviews/surveys, and training lists
constraints: The article notes audit programs and implementation interventions may need regular updating to align with updated guidelines
target_learners: Practicing nurses in hospital neurology wards
target_learning_goals: Improve nurses' knowledge, skills, and compliance with evidence-based screening, prevention, and management of poststroke depression
examples: The framework was applied in a 56-bed neurology ward of the Fifth Affiliated Hospital of Zunyi Medical University using JBI PACES software and GRiP tools.
key_sources: Tan Jing, Brancatisano Olivia, Cadilhac Dominique A., Deng Bo, Wu Yanni, Li Yan, Liu Ning. (2023). Screening, prevention, and management of patients with poststroke depression in a tertiary hospital in China: a best practice implementation project. JBI Evidence Implementation. https://doi.org/10.1097/XEB.0000000000000377
